sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Claude-Mem gives coding agents memory between sessions. A second agent takes notes while you work, and each new session starts with a short index of what matters, pulling in details only when needed.
sixtySeconds.problem: Each new agent session starts from zero, re-reading the same files and repeating mistakes you already fixed. Claude-Mem records observations as you work and brings them back in later sessions.
whoFor: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode users
Developers working on the same project over many sessions
Teams that want to share project knowledge
Anyone tired of re-explaining context to an agent
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want automatic memory across sessions with local storage by default. Note that the hosted observer option is a paid service after a free trial; you can pick another provider instead.
requirements: A supported agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more)

overview: Claude-Mem runs an observer next to your agent that writes notes while it works. The next session opens with a compact, layered index of past observations, and the agent opens full details only when it needs them, to save tokens. A mem-search skill searches project history in three steps: index, timeline and details.

The installer finds supported agents on your machine and asks which to set up. Memory is stored in ~/.claude-mem on your computer; cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are on by default and can be turned off with npx claude-mem telemetry disable. Anything wrapped in private tags is never stored.

The installer may ask you to sign in; choosing the hosted claude-mem observer starts a 30-day free trial. You can skip sign-in with an explicit --provider flag or CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false. Optional TeamBrain lets team members share selected work.
